resources.string: irc — open the native TLS IRC terminal. /server, /connect, /login, /register, /join, /window, /query, /msg and /help.
Password · masked, session only · Back cancels
Choose a username, then a masked password. We join only after your account is confirmed. Re:TUI remembers this device by default; you can turn that off below.
Use an IRC nickname: up to 30 characters, without spaces. Advanced account names can use /login.
Enter your IRC account name, then your password. This name will also be your nickname.
Choose a TLS network. Account names belong to that network. Default port: 6697.
Enter a channel such as #retui, then Continue.
IRC, at your fingertips.\nSign in, choose a channel, and talk.
Create an IRC account with a username and password. No email is required. Registration is subject to server limits.
Use an existing account on this network. Nickname-only connections and registration are available through commands where supported.
Showing the first 1,000 channels. You can still join a channel by name.
Join a channel to see its people.
1. Type a message and press ↵ to send.\n2. Tap a conversation chip to switch chats.\n3. Open Channels to find or join a channel.

TLS protects the connection, not against server operators. Private conversations are not end-to-end encrypted.\nLeaving this pane disconnects. Passwords are not saved. Unconfirmed messages are never retried automatically.
Leave %1$s? Your in-session draft will be kept.
Choose a message. You can request deletion of your own messages; channel moderators can delete other messages. The server checks permission.
Delete this message from IRC history and supported clients? Copies on Discord or other clients may remain.
Message deletion is unavailable on this connection.
This message is no longer available for deletion.
Choose a command for its syntax. Nothing is sent until you press ↵.
Reconnect automatically with a protected device key; no saved password. Anyone using your unlocked Launcher can access this account. A new phone or reinstall needs password sign-in.
Device remembered. IRC reconnects automatically when opened.
Device login could not be confirmed. Sign in with your password to retry.

Remove the login key from this phone and disconnect? Server revocation will also be requested if this account is connected. If offline, remove its old certificate through NickServ on a trusted client.
Local device key removed. Password sign-in is required. Check NickServ certificate authorization if server revocation could not complete.
Device authorization revoked and local key removed.

string-array.name: irc_commands
string-array.item: /server hostname [TLS-port] — choose a network while disconnected
/connect — connect; account login asks for a masked password
/login account — enter a masked account password
/register — guided username/password signup; connected clients use NickServ
/msg nickname text — send a private message
/window number|name|next|prev|close — switch or close a buffer
/topic [text] — view or change the channel topic
/whois nickname — ask the server about a nickname
/mode target modes — change modes where permitted
/kick nickname [reason] — remove a member where permitted
/delete — choose a channel message and confirm deletion
/oper name — enter a masked operator password

resources.string:
Native IRC terminal — one TLS network at a time.
/server [host] [TLS port] · default irc.kokodoko.cloud 6697
/nick nickname · /connect · /login account (masked SASL password)
/register (guided signup offline; masked NickServ password when connected)
/join #channel · /j #channel · /part [#channel]
/window [number|name|next|prev|close] · /buffer is an alias
/query nick · /msg nick text · /me action · /names · /list
/topic [text] · /whois nick · /mode target modes · /kick nick [reason]
/oper name (masked password) · /disconnect · /quit · /clear · /help
Plain text goes only to the active joined channel or query. //text sends /text literally. Unknown commands never become messages or launcher commands.
Window markers: * unread · ! mention/private message. Passwords are never transcript/history entries. TLS is verified; no plaintext fallback.
Register once, then sign in or reconnect before joining registered-only channels. Server-readable, not end-to-end encrypted. On supported networks, rejoining loads up to 100 recent channel messages. Server-confirmed deletions replace messages with a deletion marker. There is no push or background service; leaving disconnects. Unconfirmed messages are never retried automatically.
